title: Separation of highly hydrophilic nicotinamide metabolites using a COSMOSIL PBr column
author: Ozaki, Shimotsuma, et al.
materials: A 20 mM ammonium formate solution (pH 6.4) was prepared by dissolving 1.26 g of ammonium formate powder (M.W. 63.06 g/mol) in ultrapure water and filling up to 1 L (no need to adjust pH). The solution was suction-filtered using MILLICUP-HV filter units (pore size; 0.45 µm, Cat. No. SJHVM4710, Merck, Darmstadt, Germany).

After starting up the SHIMADZU HPLC system equipped with an LC-30 AD intelligent pump and an SPD-20AD detector (Shimadzu, Kyoto, Japan), the feed line was changed from the wash solution (ultrapure water/methanol, 1/1, vol./vol.) to solvent A and B. To prevent the wash solution and the mobile phase from mixing, solution was removed from the feed line, and a small amount of air was introduced into the feed line before putting the feed line into the mobile phase. After purging, the COSMOSIL 3PBr column (3.0 mm I.D. × 150 mm, particle size; 3 µm, Cat. No. 19352–91) was attached and equilibrated with 100% solvent A at a temperature of 40 °C and a flow rate of 0.4 mL/min for 10–15 min. A blank analysis should be performed before analyzing the sample. Each standard sample (except NAD+) was dissolved in ultrapure water to 5 mM (NAD+ was dissolved in 1 M NaOH to 5 mM). The peak shape and retention time of each standard sample should be confirmed by HPLC analysis before analyzing nicotinamide metabolites in foods.

An LTQ XL mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA) was used. The sheath gas nitrogen flow rate was set at 15 (arb), the aux gas flow rate was set at 5 (arb), and the block heater in the LC–MS equipment was heated to 400 °C. A mass range of m/z 50–1000 was covered with a scan time of 1.0 s, and data were collected in positive ion mode using a detector voltage of 1.5 kV. Nicotinamide metabolites were detected at m/z 336.5 (NAMN, M.W. 335.2), m/z 335.5 (NMN, M.W. 334.2), m/z 525.5 (ATP, M.W. 507.5, the m/z value corresponds to the ammonium ion adduct), m/z 124.5 (NA, M.W. 123.1), m/z 349.5 (IMP, M.W. 348.2), m/z 256.5 (NR, M.W. 255.5), m/z 244.5 (cytidine, M.W. 243.2), m/z 123.5 (NAM, M.W. 122.1), m/z 269.5 (inosine, M.W. 268.2), m/z 664.5 (NAD+, M.W. 663.4), and m/z 665.5 (NADH, M.W. 664.4).

steps.title: Extract Nicotinamide Metabolites from Tomato
steps.instruction: Perform liquid-liquid extraction of nicotinamide metabolites from a tomato sample.

substeps.instruction: Suspend 1 g of tomato sample in 2 mL of chloroform/methanol (1/2, vol./vol.) and 400 µL of ultrapure water.
Centrifuge the mixture at 9100 rpm for 10 min at room temperature.
Transfer 2 mL of the supernatant into an eggplant flask and dry by evaporation.
Dissolve the resulting residue with 200 µL of ultrapure water.

steps.title: Prepare Ammonium Formate Stock Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a 20 mM ammonium formate solution (pH 6.4).

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 1.26 g of ammonium formate powder (M.W. 63.06 g/mol) in ultrapure water and fill up to 1 L.
Suction-filter the solution using MILLICUP-HV filter units (pore size: 0.45 µm, Cat. No. SJHVM4710, Merck).

steps.title: Prepare Mobile Phase Solvents
steps.instruction: Prepare Solvent A and Solvent B for the HPLC system.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Solvent A (500 mL) by mixing 475 mL of the 20 mM ammonium formate solution with 25 mL of methanol.
Prepare Solvent B (500 mL) by mixing 400 mL of the 20 mM ammonium formate solution with 100 mL of methanol.

steps.title: Prepare HPLC System and Column
steps.instruction: Set up the SHIMADZU HPLC system (LC-30 AD pump and SPD-20AD detector) and equilibrate the column.

substeps.instruction: Change the feed line from wash solution (ultrapure water/methanol, 1/1, vol./vol.) to solvent A and B.
Remove solution from the feed line and introduce a small amount of air before placing the line into the mobile phase to prevent mixing.
Purge the system and attach the COSMOSIL 3PBr column (3.0 mm I.D. × 150 mm, particle size: 3 µm, Cat. No. 19352–91).
Equilibrate the column with 100% solvent A at 40 °C and a flow rate of 0.4 mL/min for 10–15 min.
Perform a blank analysis.

steps.title: Prepare Standard Samples
steps.instruction: Prepare standard samples to confirm peak shape and retention time.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve standard samples (except NAD+) in ultrapure water to a concentration of 5 mM.
Dissolve NAD+ in 1 M NaOH to a concentration of 5 mM.

steps.title: Configure LC-MS Parameters
steps.instruction: Set up the LTQ XL mass spectrometer for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Set sheath gas nitrogen flow rate to 15 (arb) and aux gas flow rate to 5 (arb).
Heat the block heater to 400 °C.
Set the mass range to m/z 50–1000 with a scan time of 1.0 s.
Collect data in positive ion mode using a detector voltage of 1.5 kV.

steps.title: Perform HPLC and LC-MS Analysis
steps.instruction: Run the separation of nicotinamide metabolites using the specified gradient and detection parameters.

substeps.instruction: Apply the following gradient for Solvent B concentration: 0% at 0 min, 0% at 5 min, 90% or 100% at 20 min, 0% at 20.1 min, and 0% at 30 min.
Perform the analytical run from 0–20 min, followed by a reequilibration process from 20.1–30 min.

Detect metabolites at the following m/z values: NAMN (336.5), NMN (335.5), ATP (525.5), NA (124.5), IMP (349.5), NR (256.5), cytidine (244.5), NAM (123.5), inosine (269.5), NAD+ (664.5), and NADH (665.5).
